scope: Does the 2D Kovasznay objective need FP64 on H100? FP64, FP32 and FP32 with TF32 matrix products for compiled Q10 (cell A) and native GL8 (cell C): replay accuracy and speed, and complete solves with unchanged FP64 acceptance
motivation: The external review asked for FP32/TF32 measurements, since most PINN users train in FP32 and the speedups may differ

source.patch_scope: dtype checks only: eight modules accept FP32 or FP64 consistently instead of FP64 only; the native extension is built for the data dtype (its existing FP32 code path). FP64 outputs are unchanged

tf32.flags: torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 and float32 matmul precision 'high'; other arms set them off and 'highest'

data_and_parameters: FP64 problem data and formal initializations are built unchanged, verified against the frozen hashes, then cast to the arm's dtype

replay.timing: bench_gpu replay measurement unchanged: 2 s warmup, 7 x 100 CUDA Graph replays timed with CUDA events, compile counters unchanged
replay.correctness: FP64 arms: bench_gpu's own dense-Q10 oracle check (atol 2e-12, rtol 2e-11). FP32 and TF32 arms: loss and gradient compared with the FP64 dense-Q10 oracle on the same parameters cast to FP64; reported, and the process fails only if a value is non-finite or the relative L2 gradient error is at least 0.1 (a sanity gate against broken kernels, not an accuracy claim)

solves.optimizer: solve.py program unchanged (4,000 Adam updates; strong-Wolfe L-BFGS blocks of 20 iterations / 25 evaluations, history 50, tolerances unchanged; 500-block extension of bench_gpu.complete_solve)
solves.precision_scope: the loss/gradient engine, parameters and optimizer state are in the arm's dtype
solves.acceptance: every stop check and the final acceptance evaluate the parameters cast to FP64 on the FP64 problem (solve.evaluate and solve.independent_metrics), with the unchanged thresholds; a solve is accepted only by this FP64 check

registered_statistics.replay_accuracy: per cell, precision and size: largest relative L2 gradient error and relative loss error against the FP64 oracle over processes
registered_statistics.replay_speed: per cell and size: FP64/FP32 and FP64/TF32 ratios of cell medians (median over processes of per-process medians) with percentile-bootstrap 95% intervals (10,000 resamples, seed 20261016); C/A within each precision
registered_statistics.solves: per cell, precision and size: accepted count and evaluations; paired over seeds and jointly accepted: FP64/FP32 and FP64/TF32 geometric means of optimization-only, per-evaluation and setup-plus-optimization time; C/A within each precision

decision_rules.training_sufficiency: for a cell, reduced precision and size: sufficient if 6/6 solves pass FP64 acceptance, insufficient if at most 4/6, otherwise unresolved
decision_rules.solve_speed: reduced precision is faster at a size if the optimization-only geometric mean of FP64/reduced exceeds 1.03 and at least 5 jointly accepted pairs exist and at least 5 of them favour the reduced arm; slower under the mirrored rule; otherwise no gain. The same rule decides C/A within each precision
decision_rules.replay_speed: a ratio counts as an effect when its bootstrap interval excludes [0.97, 1.03]

expectations.accuracy: FP32 gradients near 1e-7 relative error (CPU check of the patch: 2.6e-7 to 3.2e-7); TF32 matrix products much larger, near the TF32 unit roundoff of about 5e-4 or above
expectations.replay_speed: reduced precision helps most where pointwise work and memory traffic dominate (larger point counts); TF32 adds a GEMM speedup
expectations.solves: at 2,048 points the fixed L-BFGS cost of about 6 ms per evaluation leaves little room for any precision gain; at 65,536 points the gradient dominates and reduced precision can shorten optimization. Acceptance gates are 1-2% relative errors, so FP32 training is expected to pass; TF32 is uncertain

execution: one exclusive ACC node, four H100 lanes pulling fresh-process tasks from one pre-randomized queue; a prebuild step compiles the FP64 and FP32 native extensions once before the queue starts; deadline and fail-fast guards; no retries
